rites.name: Keluradock
rites.text: Keluradock is the concept of a tuned sounding that the Lyannae people hold to be the first note of the world's roots condensing out of the Singing. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall split the old bonds between peoples and places, the concept was said to hum through every fracture as a reminder that what was divided once sang as one.

rites.name: Telauntes
rites.text: Telauntes is the concept of the Courts in Lyannae, the principle by which trials are judged and councils bind their verdicts. In the Age of the first sovereign it was carved into the lintels of the doors between worlds, so that every crossing had to be witnessed.

rites.name: Miileneth
rites.text: Miileneth is the planting of the Weave across the Lyannae skies, when the makers sow threads of arcane pattern into the air and the quiet powers drift into slumber. The event lasts a single long dusk, during which the hum of old magic softens and then goes still. Its energy is spent gently, more like a lullaby than a blast.

rites.name: Toraiggok
rites.text: Toraiggok is the concept of the Seeding in Lyannae, the quiet interval when the makers sow the Weave into the ground of the world and the old powers lie dormant beneath it. It is remembered less as a deed than as a stillness that the later ages look back upon.

rites.name: Kaluranmaum
rites.text: Kaluranmaum is the concept of the Sundering, the moment in Lyannae's Fall when the fractured worlds split apart into drifting Shards. It is remembered as the bond that held the last sworn Pact together as the sky cracked open.

rites.name: Nuanaerae
rites.text: Nuanaerae is the concept of the Fall of Lyannae, the moment the old world's bonds snapped and its shards drifted apart. In the Era of the Record it is remembered as the hinge on which the Pact was sworn, binding the surviving Shards to a single oath.

rites.name: Thistora
rites.text: Thistora is a concept of thorned flame that the orders of Lyannae shaped into wards during the Holy Age, binding it to temple walls and the first crossings between holding districts. Its practitioners could kindle a single ward-fire strong enough to scour a bridge clean of invaders, while its lasting sanctuaries held firm against sustained siege for generations.

rites.name: Vhagorkar
rites.text: Vhagorkar is the concept of the great reckoning-wall that the orders of Lyannae raised to hold back the tidal lightning of the outer sea. In the Age of Sundering it became the symbol every landfall was measured against, a bond that men swore by and then broke.

rites.name: Torouthun
rites.text: Torouthun is the concept of branching endings in Lyannae, the principle by which each unwritten future is held apart until a choice collapses it into one. During the Age of the first sovereign, groves and kingdoms grew up around its quiet pull, and the Library was said to shelve every outcome it had not yet let become true.

rites.name: Osuramsaari
rites.text: Osuramsaari is a concept in the Lyannae Arcane Realm, held in the Three Futures where the ending branches and the Library shelves every outcome. Its nature is the sorting of possible endings, lending weight to whichever branch is chosen during the Age of Sundering. It is best known for its quiet pull on the bonds that landfall tried to break.
